judge_context: This test targets the Step-0 precondition specifically. The parentage-relevant assertions are person_evidence-linked (co-residence a_004/a_010/a_015, father-named a_013, the will a_014), while the unlinked assertions (ages a_002/a_007/a_009, birthplace a_003, death a_011, birth-year a_012) only corroborate facts already carried by linked assertions. The correct behavior is to treat them as advisory and PROCEED to evaluate exhaustiveness — NOT to halt at the precondition and defer to person-evidence.

Claude should update research.json to set q_001.search_stop.stopped_because to a stop-gate value (e.g. "question_answered") and q_001.status to 'exhaustive_declared' via research_append. Verify the write via the file_changes / after-state, not the chat text.

The search_stop.stop_criteria object must contain all seven keys: goal_alignment, repository_breadth, original_substitution, independent_verification, evidence_class, conflict_resolution, overturn_risk — each a 1-2 sentence assessment grounded in the scenario's log entries and assertions. log_entry_ids must reference the supporting log entries.

It is acceptable to note the unlinked corroborating assertions as an advisory, but that note must not prevent the declaration. A refusal to declare that cites the unlinked assertions as the blocker is a FAIL for this test.

The question is specifically about the FATHER. Thomas Flynn's will names 'my eldest son Patrick Flynn', the death certificate names Thomas as father, and Patrick is in his household in 1850, 1860 and 1870. Every plan item is closed: the later censuses, the Pottsville register and the indexed Irish baptisms were searched, and naturalization is skipped with a recorded reason. Overturn risk is low — exhaustive does not mean exhausting every record type.
